---
title: "A traceable route to the data"
subtitle: "Data availability, analytical starting points and access boundaries."
---

## One study, several data layers

The repository is the index of the analysis, not a replacement for the archives
that host the original datasets. Each figure chapter records its inputs and
analysis boundary. Source code stays in GitHub; the numerical inputs are packaged
separately in a Zenodo draft. The machine-readable
[input catalogue](https://github.com/BolisLab/mir29/blob/main/data/input-catalogue.json)
tracks the analytical starting points and access boundaries.

| Layer | What belongs here | Where it will be available |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Source code | Analysis, plotting and upstream-processing recipes | This repository |
| Public annotations | Reference sequences, assembly identifiers and aggregate metadata | Chapter data files, after review |
| Analytical checkpoints | Processed matrices and model inputs required to rerun panels | Zenodo data package v1; last confirmed as an unpublished, restricted draft on 9 October 2026 |
| Newly generated data | RNA-seq and DNA-methylation measurements and processed data | Deposited in GEO; accessions withheld from this repository until release |
| External raw datasets | Previously published measurements | Original study accessions listed in the analyses |
| Controlled metadata | Restricted participant-level phenotypes | Original access-controlled resource, not this repository |

Public source accessions are retained in the figure chapters, including the
small-RNA dataset inventory.

## Newly generated data and result exploration

The RNA-seq and DNA-methylation data generated in this study have been deposited
in GEO. Their accessions are withheld from this public-facing repository until
release. Reviewer links are provided separately to the journal and are not
stored here.

[Tabula Ages](https://tabula-ages.pages.dev) is a separate interactive resource
for exploring study results. It is currently password-protected, with reviewer
access details supplied separately. This Quarto companion documents the
analyses and their reproducibility requirements; it remains a local preview.

## Zenodo input package v1

**Last confirmed status (9 October 2026): UNPUBLISHED / RESTRICTED DRAFT.** The five input archives and the three
accompanying files (`README.txt`, `MANIFEST.json` and `SHA256SUMS.txt`) have been
uploaded and the draft saved. The reserved DOI is
[10.5281/zenodo.23266285](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23266285); it is **not active
until publication**; no public download was available at that check. Private
reviewer access is issued separately. Private preview links are not stored in
this repository, and access to the GitHub code must also be granted separately.
The deposit's current publication status has not been rechecked for this update.

| Chapter | Input archive | Compressed size |
|:--|:--|--:|
| Figure 1 + S1 | `MIR29_Figure1_S1_inputs_v1.zip` | 83.8 MB |
| Figure 2 + S2 | `MIR29_Figure2_S2_inputs_v1.zip` | 35.1 MB |
| Figure 3 + S3 | `MIR29_Figure3_S3_inputs_v1.zip` | 265.9 MB |
| Figure 4 + S4 | `MIR29_Figure4_S4_inputs_v1.zip` | 184.4 MB |
| Figure 5 + S5 | `MIR29_Figure5_S5_inputs_v1.zip` | 344.2 MB |

Sizes use decimal MB; the five archives total 913.4 MB. The
[manifest](https://github.com/BolisLab/mir29/blob/main/data/zenodo-manifest.json)
records each archive member, its purpose, byte size and SHA-256 checksum. The
[checksum list](https://github.com/BolisLab/mir29/blob/main/data/zenodo-SHA256SUMS.txt)
identifies the five archives and their accompanying documentation. Most inputs
are serialized R objects; the packages also include required tables, sequence
references and rendering assets. They contain no source-code archive.

Extract each desired ZIP **into the root of the code repository**. Its stored
paths already begin with `analyses/FigureN_and_SN/`; for example, the first archive
creates `analyses/Figure1_and_S1/data/figure1_ipsc_inputs.rds`. Do not extract it
inside a chapter's `data/` folder. If inputs are already present, compare their
hashes before merging. Consult the [reproduction guide](reproduce.qmd) before
running a chapter.

## Figure 2 sequence resources

The curated resources distinguish miR-29 precursor and mature sequences, clustered
loci and singletons, assembly-specific genomic positions, and the cg10501210
target-conservation catalogue. These resources accompany the evolutionary
analysis; they are distinct from expression count matrices and methylation arrays.

## Human data access

Some human analyses use controlled-access GTEx phenotypes. Approval of the study's
dbGaP project does not make those records redistributable. Restricted donor-level
metadata, credentials and author-specific access tokens are not included here.
Public summary statistics and source code should be distinguished from those inputs.

The withheld files are Figure 1's `data/epiclock_preds_GTEX.RDS` and Figure 4's
`data/primary/gtex_sample_metrics.rds`. Full unmodified rendering of those two
chapters still requires authorised local GTEx inputs. Aggregate summaries in
the archives do not bypass those reads in the current code.

These packages also contain source-attributed public GEO sample annotations,
processed TCGA sample/clinical records and CCLE/DepMap cell-line metadata; they
are not universally aggregate-only. Source-specific access and reuse terms
continue to apply.

## Before downloading or rerunning

Check the dataset version, genome/annotation release, expected file checksum,
sample-selection rules and matching identifiers. Aggregates, per-sample values
and raw measurements are different analytical starting points.

The manifest and checksum list support file-identity checks; they do not certify
scientific validity or data-use permissions. The draft is not a published release,
and installing these archives alone does not establish complete reproducibility.
Read the [reproduction guide](reproduce.qmd) for the remaining execution limits,
including the Figure 3 reference-PDF check that runs when `digest` is installed.
